subject: Error using parboot to estimate confidence intervals

messages.author: 1a56bdb508088d6b
messages.subject: Error using parboot to estimate confidence intervals
parts:
Hi All-

Although this is my first post to the group, I find myself searching through the archives on a regular basis. Thank you to everyone who contributes to this group! 
 
I have hit a  sticky spot in my analyses and am seeking some advice to get out. I am using the gdistsamp model to estimate densities among surveyed populations and calculate derived population estimates. The problem I am having is with using the parboot function to estimate confidence intervals for the derived parameters.

My best fit model uses a negative binomial distribution and includes an effect of year (1-4) and population (A-F) on lambda (the rest are constant). 

Using vignettes, namely Chandler (2017) distsamp, and the supplemental information from Sillett et al. (2012), I built the following script: 

# Assemble empty data frames to populate using predict()
year<-rep(1:4, length=24)
pop<-rep(c("A","B","C","D","E","F"), each=4)
nd<-cbind(year, pop)
nd<-data.frame(nd)
nd$year<-as.factor(nd$year)
nd$pop<-as.factor(nd$pop)

# Predict values for populations A-F for years 1-4
getN.hat <- function(fit) {
y <- predict(fit, newdata=nd, type="lambda")$Predicted
z <- y * area    # area is a string of areas for each population, each year
zz <- z$area.ha
return(zz)
 }

# Use parboot to estimate CI's. For final runs set nsim=200
pred.all <- parboot(gds$yearpop._NBd, statistic=getN.hat, nsim=10)

In the calculation, the estimated density is multiplied by the surveyed area ('area'; which is different for each year and population). This script runs fine and produces realistic estimations. My problem surfaces when I set the nsim>30. R does not run very long, and churns out the following error message:

Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) : 
  7 nodes produced errors; first error: object 'nd' not found

With a larger nsim value, somehow 'nd' is not found. I am not sure what the source of this error is. Hopefully, someone in the community has experienced a similar problem or another way to get at CI's. 

Thank you,
Sean Murphy

parts:
Hi Sean,

That error suggests it's an issue with running the bootstrap in parallel (the default when nsim is > 100). I won't be able to look into it until next week, but what happens if you set 'parallel = FALSE' and nsim > 100? Any errors?

Best,
Adam

parts:

Switching out of parallel worked! Thank you so much for the quick response. It is a relief to have this behind me.

Thank you!

-Sean

Sean,

I think this might be one of those cases where the ability to pass extra arguments to the `parboot` function comes in handy.  

In this case, you need to also pass the `nd` object.

Can you let me know how the following works out?

 parboot(gds$yearpop._NBd, statistic=getN.hat, nsim=200, nd = nd)
